label: 0046 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 48 windows): 0045 with an afterslip state for the January 2025 Hyuga-nada earthquake, the 2000 Izu dike removed out to 300 km and a window for the 1997 Bungo Channel slow slip event, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, eleven slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0045 with three changes from a search of the residuals for signal the models miss. The 13 January 2025 Hyuga-nada earthquake (Mw 6.77), just below the Mw 6.8 cutoff for event states, gets an afterslip state, and the 2024 Hyuga-nada state decays more slowly (Omori c = 0.05 yr). Window cross-validation is 5,631 higher on 0045's base experiment, all of it in the two windows after August 2024. Without the new state, 0045's 2024 state took up the 2025 event's afterslip and reached Mw 7.17 by May 2025, more than the Mw 7.1 earthquake. Here the 2024 state reaches Mw 7.06 and the 2025 state 6.83; their sum and the fit are about the same. The base experiment has two fixes. The 2000 Izu dike intrusion is removed within 300 km instead of 150, since its step is still 3–11 mm at 150–300 km. The 1997 Bungo Channel slow slip event gets a window of its own. Together they cut 1999–2000 residuals by 15–23% at Tokai, Kanto and Bungo and remove a dip in 1999–2000 Tokai background coupling (0.70 to 0.77). They also move the Bungo 1997 slip peak beside the other Bungo events (Mw 7.00 to 6.95) and lower Tokai 2000–05 from Mw 7.18 to 7.16. The first 44 days of 1997 are now too short to run. A looser background prior lowers cross-validation by about 5,200, so the background isn't hiding changes in coupling. After 2003 the model matches 0045. Coupling far outside −1 to 1 isn't a real value: it is episode strike-slip, or Kumamoto afterslip, divided by a small plate rate. MAP solution, no posterior SD.
